{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement the capabilities framework using the existing Fabric channel configuration hierarchy: channel capabilities apply to both peers and orderers, application capabilities apply to peers, and orderer capabilities apply to orderers.",
    "Represent capability flags as string-keyed maps and expose component-specific capability interfaces so consuming code does not perform direct version checks.",
    "Use the V1.1 capability as the initial capability value, with capability checks enforcing fail-fast behavior for unsupported binaries.",
    "Enforce the ordering-system prerequisite that orderer capabilities must be enabled before application capabilities can be enabled, preventing the initial upgrade scenario from creating a fork.",
    "Implement read-your-writes as an optional chaincode stub API that reads the transaction's pending writes before falling back to committed state, while preserving the existing read behavior for callers that do not opt in.",
    "Expose CouchDB query-performance measurement through repeatable benchmark scenarios and documented measurements rather than attempting to guarantee a single performance number independent of deployment hardware.",
    "Refactor MSP configuration construction behind interfaces while preserving protobuf serialization and compatibility with existing configtxgen-generated configurations.",
    "Replace global chaincode singletons with explicit dependencies passed through constructors or test fixtures, using interfaces where this improves isolation and testability.",
    "Generate peer and orderer configuration files for tests from a World configuration object using deterministic templates and defaults.",
    "Implement lifecycle validation information as an interface returning validation parameters for named chaincodes, including an automatically generated majority endorsement policy for the +lifecycle system chaincode."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The work targets an existing Hyperledger Fabric Go codebase with protobuf definitions, channel configuration parsing, chaincode shim APIs, lifecycle code, and established unit/integration test infrastructure.",
    "The requested increment includes production code, unit tests, relevant integration tests, documentation, and the requested organization-addition video and supporting presentation image.",
    "The referenced Gerrit changes and original design document are available as implementation guidance, but the work still requires integration into the target source tree.",
    "FAB-13523 lifecycle foundations are available or can be consumed through a stable interface; implementing the complete new lifecycle beyond the requested validation interface is out of scope.",
    "CouchDB performance work covers benchmark harnesses, representative test data, query scenarios, result collection, and usage documentation; extensive distributed performance tuning is out of scope.",
    "The organization-addition demonstration uses an existing sample Fabric network and does not require creating a new deployment platform or cloud infrastructure.",
    "Backward compatibility with existing configuration files and chaincode APIs is required unless explicitly changed by the user stories.",
    "Security review, release management, and production deployment operations are limited to implementation-level checks and tests.",
    "Effort estimates are individual contributor workdays and include normal coding, debugging, test execution, and documentation effort, but exclude waiting time for external reviews or dependencies."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Capabilities framework implementation",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement channel, application, and orderer capability configuration parsing and interfaces; add V1.1 capability definitions; integrate capability checks into peer and orderer validation paths; enforce orderer-before-application activation rules; add configuration validation, failure behavior, upgrade-path tests, and compatibility tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 25
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Optional read-your-writes chaincode API",
      "activity_description": "Extend the chaincode stub API with optional transaction-state retrieval semantics, connect the API to pending transaction writes and committed state lookup, preserve existing retrieval behavior, update shim mocks, and add unit and integration tests for reads, overwrites, deletes, and absent keys.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Running-network organization addition documentation and video",
      "activity_description": "Create a topology or process image, prepare a step-by-step procedure for adding an organization without taking the network down, record and edit a demonstration using a sample network, and validate the instructions against the demonstrated workflow.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "CouchDB query-performance measurement",
      "activity_description": "Define representative CouchDB query workloads, create or extend repeatable benchmark and data-generation tooling, capture latency and throughput measurements, document test conditions and interpretation, and add basic regression coverage for the benchmark setup.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Programmatic channel configuration construction",
      "activity_description": "Introduce MSPConfig and related configuration-construction interfaces, adapt existing configuration consumers and serialization paths, preserve configtxgen compatibility, implement validation and error handling, and add unit and integration tests for constructing and encoding channel configuration blocks outside configtxgen.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Removal of chaincode singletons",
      "activity_description": "Inventory chaincode-related global singletons, define explicit lifecycle and dependency ownership, refactor production callers to use injected instances or interfaces, update initialization and shutdown behavior, repair existing tests, and add isolation and parallel-execution tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "World-driven peer and orderer test configuration",
      "activity_description": "Implement deterministic generation of peer core.yaml and orderer.yaml test configurations from World configuration values, define defaults and overrides, integrate generation into test setup, and add tests covering multiple organizations, nodes, and customized values.",
      "most_likely_effort": 8
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Lifecycle validation-parameter interface",
      "activity_description": "Implement the lifecycle interface for retrieving chaincode validation parameters, add special handling for +lifecycle, generate its majority-of-organizations signature policy, connect the interface to validation consumers, and add tests for ordinary chaincodes, lifecycle itself, missing definitions, and policy serialization.",
      "most_likely_effort": 15
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration, regression testing, and final documentation",
      "activity_description": "Run full unit, integration, and regression suites; resolve interactions among configuration, lifecycle, shim, and test infrastructure changes; update developer and administrator documentation; perform code cleanup and final acceptance verification.",
      "most_likely_effort": 10
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 116
  }
}
message.reasoning:
**Assessing capabilities and refactor plans**

I’m thinking that U1 needs capabilities like channel config, peer/orderer enforcement, config validation, upgrade guard, and tests, totaling around 25. For U6, there’s a broad singleton refactor, which I’m estimating at about 20. Alright, that gives me a clearer numerical perspective on these tasks. I guess it’s all about prioritizing what's necessary and getting organized!

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the capabilities framework using the existing Fabric channel configuration hierarchy: channel capabilities apply to both peers and orderers, application capabilities apply to peers, and orderer capabilities apply to orderers.
Represent capability flags as string-keyed maps and expose component-specific capability interfaces so consuming code does not perform direct version checks.
Use the V1.1 capability as the initial capability value, with capability checks enforcing fail-fast behavior for unsupported binaries.
Enforce the ordering-system prerequisite that orderer capabilities must be enabled before application capabilities can be enabled, preventing the initial upgrade scenario from creating a fork.

Implement read-your-writes as an optional chaincode stub API that reads the transaction's pending writes before falling back to committed state, while preserving the existing read behavior for callers that do not opt in.

Expose CouchDB query-performance measurement through repeatable benchmark scenarios and documented measurements rather than attempting to guarantee a single performance number independent of deployment hardware.
Refactor MSP configuration construction behind interfaces while preserving protobuf serialization and compatibility with existing configtxgen-generated configurations.
Replace global chaincode singletons with explicit dependencies passed through constructors or test fixtures, using interfaces where this improves isolation and testability.
Generate peer and orderer configuration files for tests from a World configuration object using deterministic templates and defaults.

Implement lifecycle validation information as an interface returning validation parameters for named chaincodes, including an automatically generated majority endorsement policy for the +lifecycle system chaincode.
assumptions: The work targets an existing Hyperledger Fabric Go codebase with protobuf definitions, channel configuration parsing, chaincode shim APIs, lifecycle code, and established unit/integration test infrastructure.
The requested increment includes production code, unit tests, relevant integration tests, documentation, and the requested organization-addition video and supporting presentation image.
The referenced Gerrit changes and original design document are available as implementation guidance, but the work still requires integration into the target source tree.
FAB-13523 lifecycle foundations are available or can be consumed through a stable interface; implementing the complete new lifecycle beyond the requested validation interface is out of scope.
CouchDB performance work covers benchmark harnesses, representative test data, query scenarios, result collection, and usage documentation; extensive distributed performance tuning is out of scope.
The organization-addition demonstration uses an existing sample Fabric network and does not require creating a new deployment platform or cloud infrastructure.
Backward compatibility with existing configuration files and chaincode APIs is required unless explicitly changed by the user stories.
Security review, release management, and production deployment operations are limited to implementation-level checks and tests.
Effort estimates are individual contributor workdays and include normal coding, debugging, test execution, and documentation effort, but exclude waiting time for external reviews or dependencies.

Extend the chaincode stub API with optional transaction-state retrieval semantics, connect the API to pending transaction writes and committed state lookup, preserve existing retrieval behavior, update shim mocks, and add unit and integration tests for reads, overwrites, deletes, and absent keys.
